preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 10000
preconditions.description: The first line contains integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) and m (0 ≤ m ≤ 10000), representing the number of planets and wormholes, respectively.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:m+1])
preconditions.description: The next m lines contain pairs of integers u and v (1 ≤ u, v ≤ n), representing undirected edges between planets.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()[m+1].split()) == 4 and all(1 <= int(x) <= 1000 for x in stdin.splitlines()[m+1].split()[0:2]) and all(0 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in stdin.splitlines()[m+1].split()[2:4])
preconditions.description: The next line contains integers s (1 ≤ s ≤ 1000), b (1 ≤ b ≤ 1000), k (0 ≤ k ≤ 10^9), and h (0 ≤ h ≤ 10^9), representing the number of spaceships, bases, gold per attacked base, and cost to create a dummy base, respectively.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and 1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n and all(0 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in line.split()[1:3]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[m+2:m+2+s])
preconditions.description: The next s lines contain three integers x (1 ≤ x ≤ n), a (0 ≤ a ≤ 10^9), and f (0 ≤ f ≤ 10^9), representing the location, attack strength, and fuel of each spaceship.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and 1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[m+2+s:m+2+s+b])
preconditions.description: The next b lines contain two integers x (1 ≤ x ≤ n) and d (0 ≤ d ≤ 10^9), representing the location and defense strength of each base.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the minimum gold lost by the rebels after optimally creating dummy bases.

The output is the minimum gold lost, calculated as the cost of creating dummy bases to cover unused ships (each dummy base costs h gold) plus the cost of attacking real bases (each attacked base costs k gold). The calculation ensures that the maximum number of real bases are attacked, and the remaining ships are assigned to dummy bases to minimize total cost.
